scenarioStory.history: 8-year-old with type 1 diabetes diagnosed at age 5. Mother reports he received his scheduled rapid-acting insulin dose at lunch today but skipped his usual afternoon snack while at a friend's house. He came home tremulous, sweaty, and irritable, telling his mother he feels 'really hungry and shaky.' Mother checked his home glucometer, which read 42 mg/dL, and called 911.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find an 8-year-old male seated at the kitchen table, conscious, tremulous, and diaphoretic. He is anxious but able to speak in full sentences and follow commands. → Oral glucose given: Crew confirms hypoglycemia with a glucometer check and administers oral glucose gel dosed to the patient's weight, appropriate for a conscious patient able to protect his airway. → IV dextrose given: Repeat blood glucose remains low and symptoms persist after oral glucose, so the crew establishes IV access and administers weight-based dextrose per protocol. → Improved, transport: Blood glucose and mental status have normalized following IV dextrose. The patient is reassessed and prepared for transport given his history of symptomatic hypoglycemia.

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find an 8-year-old male seated at the kitchen table, conscious, tremulous, and diaphoretic. He is anxious but able to speak in full sentences and follow commands.

scenarioEvents.name: Oral glucose given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew confirms hypoglycemia with a glucometer check and administers oral glucose gel dosed to the patient's weight, appropriate for a conscious patient able to protect his airway.
relatedChecklist: Check blood glucose level with glucometer
Oral glucose gel 12.5 g PO (25 kg × 0.5 g/kg)

scenarioEvents.name: IV dextrose given
scenarioEvents.description: Repeat blood glucose remains low and symptoms persist after oral glucose, so the crew establishes IV access and administers weight-based dextrose per protocol.
relatedChecklist: Recheck BGL after oral dose; confirm still 45 mg/dL with persistent symptoms
Dextrose 12.5 g IV as 125 mL D10% (25 kg × 5 mL/kg = 125 mL)
Use D10% concentration rather than higher-concentration dextrose for this pediatric patient

scenarioEvents.name: Improved, transport
scenarioEvents.description: Blood glucose and mental status have normalized following IV dextrose. The patient is reassessed and prepared for transport given his history of symptomatic hypoglycemia.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vitals and mental status; transport given continued symptomatic hypoglycemia today

scenarioEvents.name: BGL recheck skipped
scenarioEvents.description: After oral glucose, the crew does not recheck blood glucose or reassess mental status. Persistent, unrecognized hypoglycemia continues, and the patient becomes more tremulous, tachycardic, and confused.
relatedChecklist: Recognize worsening hypoglycemia; recheck BGL and reassess mental status immediately
